The raw_customers table holds 230 rows for 200 distinct customers. 200 rows are current (is_current=True, valid_from 2025-01-01) and 30 are historical (is_current=False, valid_from 2023-06-01). This is an SCD2 dimension. Joining silver_transactions to all rows duplicates transactions for the 30 customers that have history, which explains 5353 vs 4630.

The fix is to keep only current rows in silver_customers. Each customer has exactly one current row (200 current rows across 200 distinct customers), so the join is then one-to-one.

An alternative is a point-in-time join. The historical rows have valid_from 2023-06-01 and the current rows have 2025-01-01. All transactions are in January 2026, which is after both valid_from dates, so the current row is the right one for every transaction. There is no valid_to column, so the current-row filter is the clear choice.

The region value could differ in case or whitespace, but upper() is already applied. The distinct region count is 4, so that is fine.

The fix replaces silver_customers with a version filtered to is_current. The output columns stay the same.
